title: TrainingPlan
description: A periodized, multi-week strength training plan for one athlete. Extends the original Neil Burdock plan schema to also cover flexible/autoregulated plans (no pre-decided weekly weights), warm-up/primer slots, and non-integer rep prescriptions (ranges, durations, AMRAP). One unified shape for both styles: a flat list of exercise entries, one entry per exercise, per training day, per week.

athlete.description: Name or identifier of the athlete this plan was built for.

generated_date.description: ISO 8601 date the plan was generated/exported.

weeks_total.description: Total number of weeks covered by the plan.

model_name.description: NEW (extension). The underlying training model/template this plan follows, e.g. "Model1-3x" — for plans generated by a recurring, reused template. Optional: omit entirely for one-off plans that aren't part of a named recurring model.

cycle_number.description: NEW (extension). Which iteration of model_name this is. Optional, and meaningless without model_name also being set.

target_priority_regions.description: Body regions this plan is designed to prioritize/specialize in. Use an empty array if the plan has no specific regional specialization focus.

peaking_focus.description: NEW (extension). For plans peaking specific LIFTS rather than body regions in general — a different, more specific concept from target_priority_regions. Optional: omit for plans without a specific peaking lift (e.g. Neil's region-based specialization plan doesn't use this).

label.description: The lift(s) this plan is peaking, freeform.

replaces.description: What this peaking focus replaces from a prior cycle, if anything.

reason.description: Why this peaking focus was chosen, e.g. an injury constraint driving the substitution.
examples: Squat and Deadlift excluded due to back injury (no hip hinge / spinal flexion under load); axial loading is tolerated.

constraints.description: Exercise or equipment exclusions applied when generating the plan. Use an empty array if there are none.

exercises.description: Flat list of exercise prescriptions. One entry = one exercise, on one day, in one week. For a flexible/autoregulated plan (no pre-decided weekly weights), repeat the same prescription identically across every week within a phase — see ExerciseEntry.target_weight_kg and weight_status.

week.description: Week number within the overall plan (1-indexed). For a flexible/autoregulated phase, generate one entry per week within that phase's duration, all identical except this field — do not invent per-week weight progression that wasn't actually decided.

mesocycle.description: Which periodization block this week belongs to. Free text — common values are Accumulation, Intensification, Peak, Deload, but any phase label is valid.

day_num.description: Training day number within the week (1-indexed, in weekly training order).

day_label.description: Name of the training day / session split.

series.description: Exercise slot letter within the day, in performed order (A = first). A numeric suffix (e.g. "A1", "A2") denotes a superset pair sharing the same primary slot. EXTENDED: the literal "SIT" is also allowed, denoting an optional warm-up/primer slot performed before the lettered slots.

slot_role.description: The training purpose of this slot. EXTENDED: added "Warm-up/primer" for SIT-series entries. Primary/Secondary compound slots are the load-bearing lifts tracked for progression; Accessory/Finisher slots are volume/isolation work; Warm-up/primer slots are optional preparatory work, not tracked for progression.

exercise_name.description: Exercise name, following the gym's naming convention (movement – equipment – grip/angle – stance/variant).

body_region.description: Primary body region trained by this exercise.

target_priority.description: True if body_region is one of the plan's target_priority_regions. Derived from target_priority_regions — set false for all entries if the plan has no regional specialization focus.

reps.description: EXTENDED: target reps per set, now supporting four shapes instead of only a plain integer. (1) A plain integer for a fixed rep target. (2) A range string like "8-10". (3) A duration string like "30s" for time-based work (planks, carries, bike intervals). (4) The literal string "MAX" for an all-out effort set (e.g. max chin-ups), with no numeric target.

tempo.description: 4-digit tempo code: eccentric / pause-at-bottom / concentric / pause-at-top, in seconds. 'X' means explosive/as-fast-as-possible for that phase.

rest_sec.description: Rest between sets, in seconds. Always a bare integer — convert source strings like "90s" to 90 at authoring time.

target_weight_kg.description: Prescribed working weight in kilograms, or the string "TBD" if the weight has not yet been set (see weight_status for why). Always a bare number, never a unit-suffixed string — convert source values like "10kg" to 10 at authoring time.

weight_status.description: Explains the state of target_weight_kg. EXTENDED: added the autoregulated case as a documented example — use this when the plan intentionally leaves the weight to be decided live at the gym (e.g. an autoregulated ramp), as opposed to a weight that is merely pending a future block's results.
examples: Pending — set from Accumulation block performance
Pending — set from Intensification block performance
Pending — set from Peak block performance
Set live at the gym (autoregulated — no pre-planned weekly weight)

weight_basis.description: How the underlying 1RM used to calculate target_weight_kg was determined. Only meaningful once target_weight_kg is a number, not "TBD". OPTIONAL (was required in the original schema) — omit entirely for autoregulated entries where target_weight_kg is always "TBD" by design, since there is no estimate basis to report.

confidence.description: Confidence in the weight_basis estimate. High = directly measured; Medium = inferred from a closely related exercise; Low = heuristic estimate with no directly comparable logged data. OPTIONAL (was required in the original schema) — omit for autoregulated entries, same reasoning as weight_basis.

notes.description: NEW (extension). Freeform coaching notes for this specific exercise entry, e.g. form cues, injury-related cautions, or context on why this exercise was chosen.
examples: Start light — new-ish loading pattern for you; back fully supported, no hinge
